name: Ganang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page for gana1270 Ganang (copy consulted) and the our source list record: three refs (Shimizu 1975 overview, ISO 2007-147, Blench 2006 wordlist), Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology.
sources.note: Bibliographic only; no descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference exists for Ganang.

sources.citation: Crossref works query 'Ganang Gashish Izere Plateau Nigeria' (10 hits, all non-linguistic).
sources.note: No published journal article on Ganang exists in Crossref.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An atlas of Nigerian languages, 4th ed. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 210 'Izere cluster' (*Ganang — Source: Blench (2006)); index line 'Ganang – dialect of Izere', 'Gashish – dialect of Berom'.
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic only. Names Blench 2006/2016 ms. 'The Ganang Language of Central Nigeria and its Affinities' as the sole source for Ganang.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. Research on the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Uebersee 93: 1-49.
sources.note: Nothing on Ganang beyond one comparative wordlist row ('Ganang i-nsɛŋ' for 'smoke'); no phonological statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012 [Glottolog lists it as 2006]. The Ganang language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout 13 May 2012, 24 pp. (wordlist collected at Gashish Kuk, 18 Jan 2001, with Selbut Longtau). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, electronic ms.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (full text searched for stress|accent|prominen|suprasegment|pitch: only the tone-diacritic table). Section 3 'Phonology' (pp. 2-3), explicitly 'tentative': 7 vowels, consonant chart, 3.3 Tones: 'There are five tones in Ganang, three level and two contour tones. Contour tones occur in loanwords, words with potentially onomatopoeic names such as those of birds and where a tonally dissimilar VV sequence has been shortened' (p. 3). Intro says 'In general, tones are not marked' in the wordlist.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. [2008 printout]. The Ganang language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Earlier version of the same wordlist paper (old rogerblench.info path.%20dialects/Ganang%).
sources.note: Earlier draft of the one existing description; the Internet Archive copy (20081202154914) is truncated server-side (130,700 of ~251,000 bytes) and could not be read. Almost certainly the same phonology text; would only confirm no stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-147: split [fiz] Izere into [izr] Izere and [gne] Ganang (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International, 8 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; repeats Blench's sentence that Ganang phonology and noun classes have taken on Berom features; cites only Blench's 2001 minority-languages list.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The strange case of Ganang. 1-page sociolinguistic note (Word doc dated 3 Jan 2006), rogerblench.info.
sources.note: Nothing; only 'Linguistically, Ganang turns out to be a form of Izere that has been Beromised. The phonology and noun-class system have taken on features of Berom and it is for practical purposes unintelligible to mainstream Izere.'

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2001 field recordings of the Ganang 400-item wordlist (taped; 'tones.. will be added when time permits').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only primary data on Ganang; unpublished audio held by the author. Any future phonology (tone or prominence) would have to come from this or new fieldwork.

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1975. The languages of Jos Division (Linguistic Survey of Plateau State, Part I). Kano: Centre for the Study of Nigerian Languages, Ahmadu Bello University. 27 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only other item Glottolog lists for Ganang; a survey listing of Jos Division languages that may carry a wordlist or classification note on Gashish/Ganang, though unlikely to discuss stress.
